children: is limiting redemptions from its flagship private credit fund for the third straight quarter after investors sought to withdraw shares equivalent to 14.7% of the fund, according to a regulatory filing Tuesday.

Apollo Debt Solutions BDC, which had about $25.9B in assets, will repurchase up to 5% of its outstanding shares under its quarterly limit. The latest redemption requests were down from 16.8% in Q2 but remained well above the amount the fund can repurchase.

The asset manager said redemption requests declined sequentially among both U.S. onshore and offshore investors. The fund estimated that the vast majority of Q3 requests came from investors re-tendering shares that were not repurchased in prior quarters, rather than from new withdrawal requests.

The latest tender marks another quarter in which investor demand for liquidity has exceeded the fund’s repurchase capacity. Apollo has continued to work through the backlog of redemption requests while maintaining the 5% quarterly limit. Apollo
estimated that the latest repurchase would result in about $700M of gross outflows, according to a September 22 letter to shareholders.

title: Apollo caps private credit fund redemptions for third straight quarter
